slice_results.code_snippet:
#!/bin/sh -x
set -e

SRC="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/g200kg/webaudio-tinysynth/master/webaudio-tinysynth.js"
OUT="webaudio-tinysynth.js"

curl $SRC -o $OUT


MOD="if (module) module.exports = WebAudioTinySynth"
MSG="// Original source: $SRC"

echo "\n\n$MOD\n$MSG\n" >> $OUT
slice_results.behavior_summary: During installation, the shell script executes the curl command to download a JavaScript file from the hardcoded URL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/g200kg/webaudio-tinysynth/master/webaudio-tinysynth.js and saves it locally as webaudio-tinysynth.js. It then appends module export code and a comment referencing the original source URL to the downloaded file, modifying the local file system. This behavior enables remote code retrieval and local file modification, potentially facilitating supply chain compromise or execution of externally hosted code.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The analyzed script downloads a JavaScript source file from a well-known public GitHub repository and appends a module export statement along with a comment referencing the original source. Unlike the known malicious patterns, it does not execute the downloaded code, does not download binaries or scripts from suspicious or untrusted domains, and does not run any commands that would lead to arbitrary code execution or system compromise. The use of curl to fetch a publicly available source file and modifying it locally is a common practice in legitimate build or packaging scripts. There is no evidence of obfuscation, execution of downloaded content, or network requests to suspicious domains. Therefore, while the script performs remote code retrieval and local file modification, these actions alone do not constitute malicious behavior.
